name: Zone 2 cardio

lead: Zone 2 is steady, easy-to-moderate cardio at a pace where conversation remains possible. People use it as a low-stress way to burn calories and support fat loss for a leaner look without cutting into training recovery.

At low intensity the body relies mostly on fat for fuel, with more glycogen used as intensity rises. It is popular in fitness and longevity circles, and zone-specific trials for appearance goals have not been published in the sources reviewed.

paras: Users do 30 to 60 minute sessions of walking, cycling, jogging or rowing at a conversational pace, measured by heart rate or the ability to talk, several times a week alongside lifting.
General aerobic exercise is considered low-risk; people with health conditions are generally advised to consult a clinician.

forums.title: When I grow up, I want to be an Alicorn

angle.text: Easy, steady cardio burns extra calories with little fatigue, so you can add it on top of training to lower body fat and look leaner. It is popular in fitness circles, and zone-specific research for appearance goals is limited.

lead: Zone 2 cardio refers to low-to-moderate intensity steady aerobic exercise, in popular heart-rate-zone schemes the second zone, often described as a pace at which conversation remains possible. It has become popular in fitness and longevity communities and is discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a low-stress way to burn fat.

Encyclopedic sources describe aerobic exercise as repeated light-to-moderate activity over extended periods, with fat and glycogen as the main fuels and relatively more fat used at lower intensity.[1] The Zone 2 label itself is not defined in the sources reviewed, and no published trials were reviewed on it.

paras: Aerobic exercise guidance recommends about 2.5 hours a week of moderate activity to lower health risks, and even about 11 minutes a day has been associated with lower risk of early death, with high-intensity interval training possibly giving similar benefits in less time.[1]

At lower intensities the body relies mainly on fat, shifting toward glycogen as intensity rises; the same source notes that low-to-moderate exercise is not very efficient for fat loss per unit time compared with high-intensity exercise, though that passage is flagged as needing verification.[1]
No studies found specific to Zone 2 as a named protocol. General evidence on aerobic exercise is summarised under its own topic.[1]
